outputs.explanation: Panel A is a schematic diagram of breast anatomy plus a classification table; it contains no data plot requiring individual data points.
Panel B is a schematic illustrating the study's conceptual aim, not a data plot.
Panel C is a schematic depicting the experimental method (luciferase recordings), not a data plot.
Panel D is a schematic; the sinusoidal curves shown are idealized illustrations of the analysis concept, not measured data requiring individual points.
Panel E is a schematic illustrating the concept of correlation analysis; the heatmap shown is an illustrative example, not actual data, and heatmaps in general don't require individual points.
Panel F is a schematic of the growth-dynamics workflow; the growth curve shown is an idealized illustration (a line plot type, which is exempt regardless), not real averaged data.
Panel G is a schematic of the drug-sensitivity workflow; the dose-response curve is an idealized illustration (line plot, exempt), not real averaged data with replicates to show.
Panel H is a schematic of the genomic analysis workflow; the heatmap and mutation grid are illustrative examples (heatmaps are exempt), not actual quantified averages.

Panel I is a schematic illustrating the concept of subtype clustering; the PCA and 3D scatter plots are illustrative examples of individual points/clusters themselves (scatter plots are exempt) rather than bar/summary charts needing overlaid raw data.
